page: Amazon Web Services t4g.micro is an entry-tier burstable cloud server belonging to the Graviton processor family. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and features the arm64 architecture utilizing AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates two physical cores presenting two single-threaded vCPUs and 1.0 GB of system memory, resulting in 0.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache distribution includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via dedicated AES instruction support, while x86 vector extensions and simultaneous multithreading are absent. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated graphics accelerators, relying exclusively on network-attached elastic block storage.

Benchmark analysis reflects the burstable and constrained hardware profile of the instance. In stress-ng evaluations, single-core CPU throughput registers in the average range, whereas multi-core compute metrics place in the bottom quartile due to strict CPU credit throttling and a low core count. Synthetic memory bandwidth evaluations indicate restrained transfer speeds, measuring 116.9 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 34.19 GB/sec for larger 256 MB reads. Compression evaluations exhibit lower-tier scores, with single-threaded gzip reaching 20.31 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 12.71 GB/sec. Across PassMark evaluation suites, overall CPU, memory, and database operational metrics consistently measure within the lower deciles, matching the low throughput recorded in Redis operations and static web serving benchmarks.

From an infrastructure perspective, t4g.micro delivers qualitative cost efficiency by maintaining an exceptionally small resource footprint designed around intermittent CPU utilization. The shared-core credit system permits temporary bursts of processing speed while economizing resource consumption during idle intervals. However, the 1.0 GB memory envelope and absence of dedicated local storage limit operation of concurrent applications. The t4g.micro instance is appropriately aligned with non-critical workloads such as microservices, small development and testing environments, remote monitoring agents, lightweight cron tasks, and low-traffic administrative dashboards that do not sustain continuous CPU or memory pressure.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.micro is an entry-tier burstable virtual machine powered by AWS Graviton2 processors built on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 architecture. Operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides two burstable physical cores running at 2.5 GHz without hyperthreading, alongside 1.0 GB of system memory. The instance includes 32 MB of shared L3 cache and hardware-assisted AES cryptography, while omitting bundled local storage and dedicated GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate average single-core performance in stress-ng evaluations, contrasted by lower throughput across multi-core tests, memory bandwidth benchmarks, and compressed data processing. Due to its constrained memory capacity and burstable CPU credit allocation, the server exhibits lower rankings in high-concurrency database operations and throughput tests. The t4g.micro offers a cost-efficient footprint suited for lightweight continuous integration tasks, development environments, low-traffic web services, health-check monitors, and small administrative scripting workloads that experience periodic execution demands.
